It is worth noting that Millau is characterized by significant daily temperature fluctuations in most months. The difference between average maximum and minimum temperatures is often around 10-11°C, especially in the summer and transitional months. For example, in July, the average maximum is 25.3°C, while the minimum is 14.3°C. This means that even after a warm day, the evening and night can be significantly cooler, which is worth considering when planning activities and choosing clothing.

Average monthly temperature

## Precipitation [...] Summers in Millau are usually warm and pleasant. Daytime temperatures in June, July, and August often rise above 20°C, peaking in mid-summer. Nights remain relatively cool, especially in early summer, with minimum temperatures around 12-14°C, ensuring a comfortable sleep. In contrast, winter is cool but not severe. Average daytime temperatures from December to February range from 6°C to 8.7°C, while nighttime temperatures drop close to or slightly above zero, especially in January (0.2°C) and February (0.9°C). [...] ## Temperature

The climate in Millau is characterized by noticeable seasonal temperature fluctuations. Throughout the year, the average temperature varies from a cool 3.1°C in January to a comfortable 19.8°C in July and August. The hottest months are typically July and August, when average maximum temperatures reach 25.3°C and 25.4°C respectively, and average minimum temperatures stay around 14.3°C. The coldest period falls in January, with an average minimum temperature of about 0.2°C and a maximum of around 6.0°C.

## Overview

The climate in **Millau** is best described as *temperate*, with four distinct seasons. The city offers a variety of weather conditions throughout the year, allowing you to choose the optimal time for your trip based on your preferences. Summers here are warm and quite sunny, while winters are cool but without extreme frosts.

The summer months, especially **July and August**, are the warmest, with average temperatures around 19.8°C and maximums reaching 25°C. Notably, these are also the driest months, with minimal precipitation (only 1-2 mm) and the fewest rainy days. Winter, from December to February, brings cool weather with average temperatures between 3°C and 5°C, and nighttime temperatures can drop close to freezing. Spring and autumn are transitional seasons with mild and pleasant weather, although precipitation is slightly higher than in summer, it remains low (2-3 mm per month). The number of rainy days is more evenly distributed throughout the year, except for the summer months, indicating the possibility of brief showers.

## Temperature

The climate in **Millau** is characterized by noticeable seasonal temperature fluctuations. Throughout the year, the average temperature varies from a cool 3.1°C in January to a comfortable 19.8°C in July and August. The hottest months are typically July and August, when average maximum temperatures reach 25.3°C and 25.4°C respectively, and average minimum temperatures stay around 14.3°C. The coldest period falls in January, with an average minimum temperature of about 0.2°C and a maximum of around 6.0°C.

title: Temperatures on the Earth's surface: new records broken in France ...
content: To understand recent temperature trends, natural phenomena such as variations in solar radiation, major volcanic eruptions and the El Niño phenomenon must be taken into account. Added to this is the anthropogenic contribution linked to the accumulation of greenhouse gases. In 2025, the sun was at its peak activity in its approximately 11-year cycle, there were no volcanic eruptions intense enough to cool the atmosphere, and it was a neutral period in terms of El Niño/La Niña. However, greenhouse gas concentrations are not yet falling, despite the efforts of many countries to reduce emissions. When all these factors are taken into account, it is clear that 2025 was the second hottest year since the IASI sounder began flying.

# Temperatures on the Earth’s surface: new records broken in France in 2025

---

Temperatures measured in France in 2025 broke new records according to observations provided by the French IASI sounder aboard the Metop satellite. This was particularly true for surface temperatures, which are the best indicator for monitoring climate change. Unlike more traditional meteorological data, which measures temperature at an altitude of 2 metres, the observations provided by this atmospheric sounder give the same measurements as if a thermometer were plunged directly into the ground or water. And this is true on land and at sea, with an accuracy exceeding 0.1°C.

![Température de surface IASI de 2008 à 2025 - France. D. R.](https://www.ipsl.fr/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/temp-surface-iasi_2026-01-08.png)
